plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive 1v1 fold changes
plan.analytical_narrative: The inputs are a 12,000 x 3 raw integer gene-level count CSV from salmon (first column gene symbol, one column per sample) and a 2 x 2 sample table with a condition column: exactly one treated sample and one control sample of human liver. The research question asks which genes are differentially expressed between them. With one sample per condition there is no within-group replication, so no dispersion can be estimated and no p-value from this design has an inferential basis. The knowledge service returns this as a hard flag (R-0003@6b3a: descriptive_only), and it drops the shrinkage and multiple-testing steps entirely. The plan therefore does what the data can support and refuses what it cannot: QC of the two libraries (T1S1), then median-of-ratios normalization, the standard low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 1 sample, the smallest group size here), and a DESeq2 object built with condition as a two-level factor with control set explicitly as the reference level, from which descriptive log2 fold changes of treated over control are computed on normalized counts with a pseudocount (T1S2). No Wald test, no LRT, no p-values, no FDR — the results table has no significance column, and the ranking is by effect size with expression level reported beside it so that a large ratio from a low-count gene is visible as such. Because the gene-level statistic carries no uncertainty, the enrichment (T2S1) is likewise descriptive: fgsea preranked on the descriptive log2 fold change against human MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome/WikiPathways as follow-up, with the set-level p-values reported as a ranking device only and never as evidence. The final step (T1S3) assembles the reproducibility record and states plainly, at the top of the report, that this design does not support differential expression inference and what design would: at minimum three biological replicates per condition, which is what turns these descriptive ratios into testable hypotheses. The output of this run is a hypothesis-generating candidate list, not a differential expression result.

Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 1 sample (smallest group size = 1)

Descriptive log fold changes only, no inferential test
fgsea preranked GSEA ranked by the descriptive log2 fold change, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome; descriptive, no set-level p-value as evidence
Reproducibility record and descriptive-only narrative with the replication caveat

The design required for inference (>=3 biological replicates per condition) is named explicitly
Method, package versions, filter thresholds, size factors, contrast direction and reference level, and the number of genes surviving the filter are all reported
The enrichment section reports collection name and version, ranking metric, universe and size window, and leading-edge genes per reported set
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed and the gene set collection version is included with the results
An explicit list of what was not produced (p-values, adjusted p-values, FDR gene list, shrunken LFCs) and why appears in the report
constraints: Do not present any descriptive log2 fold change as a differentially expressed gene
Do not report a set-level p-value as evidence of a pathway change
State the enrichment method-dependence caveat
Report the reproducibility record alongside the results, not as a separate note
caveats: The temptation in a report like this is to soften the limitation into a footnote; resist it — the limitation is the primary finding
